title: 'You used me': Teens tell judge how man lured them over Snapchat, as he pleads guilty
summary: Three years after Hammad Shaikh lured and sexually assaulted underage girls he met on Snapchat, the 26-year-old pleaded guilty to seven offences and sat expressionless in a Calgary courtroom as…

image.caption: Hammad Shaikh, 26, pleaded guilty to offences involving the luring and sexual abuse of underage girls he targeted on Snapchat. (AP)

blocks.text: Calgary

Three years after Hammad Shaikh lured and sexually assaulted underage girls he met on Snapchat, the 26-year-old pleaded guilty to seven offences and sat expressionless in a Calgary courtroom as several of his victims delivered statements with what the judge described as “maturity, grace, kindness and bravery.”
Hammad Shaikh sentenced to 11.5 years in prison

Shaikh was mid-trial on 28 charges when he changed course and pleaded guilty to seven offences on Thursday involving victims between the ages of 12 and 16 years old. A publication ban protects the identities of the girls.
Justice Eleanor Funk accepted the prosecutors’ and defence lawyers’ joint proposal for an 11.5-year prison sentence.
“I hope you understand how damaging your conduct has been,” said the judge.

Details of Shaikh's crimes against the teens come from an agreed statement of facts prepared by prosecutors Sarah Goard-Baker and Stephanie Morton, and defence lawyers Rebecca Snukal and Mary Stephensen.
'I miss the person I was'
Several of the teenage girls, their loved ones and victim support workers were in court for Shaikh’s pleas and sentencing.
In a powerful and emotional display, three of the girls stood before their abuser in the courtroom and read aloud their victim impact statements.
“My view on intimacy is completely distorted now,” said VK, one of the girls lured and abused by Shaikh.

items: Trial begins for Calgary man accused of sexually assaulting underage girls he met on Snapchat

blocks.text: VK was 13 years old when Shaikh initiated contact over Snapchat. Their interactions lasted for months.
“I miss the person that I was before,” she said in court on Thursday.
“I really feel bad for my dad, though … I knew it would break his heart. I knew he would blame himself. None of it was his fault, nor was it mine.”
Victim had just lost parent
Court heard that in January 2024, Shaikh picked up VK, bought her flavoured vodka and marijuana and had sex with her in his car.
“I have no idea what my boundaries are because two years ago they were stomped on and run over," she said in court.
Another victim, LW, told the court that when she met Shaikh in the spring of 2023 she was “already hurting deeply from the loss of a parent.”
Shaikh gave LW alcohol and marijuana before he not only engaged in sexual activity with her in his car, but also recorded and saved videos of it.
'An immense amount of shame'
Shaikh admitted Thursday that he knew LW was 15 years old when he began messaging her on Instagram and Snapchat.
“I carried an immense amount of shame,” said LW. “I felt ashamed of every kiss, every touch, every word.”
“You used me in so many ways.”
More videos taken
In her statement, PC told the court that after she was victimized by Shaikh, she tried to take her own life.
Shaikh knew PC was 14 years old when he first made contact over Snapchat.
Over the next five months, he supplied marijuana and alcohol when the two met regularly and had sex in his car, home and a hotel room.
Shaikh again took videos that constituted child sexual abuse and exploitation material.
In the aftermath, PC said she suffered serious mental health issues, lost friends and stopped going to school.
“I smoked more weed and drank dangerous amounts to forget,” said PC. “I couldn't forgive myself.”
'A hurting child'
PC’s mother also read a statement, describing midnight ER visits and watching her daughter “wither away.”
“She could not be left alone … I had to focus on keeping my child alive,” said PC’s mother.
“A hurting child hurts the whole family.”
After Shaikh was first arrested, he was released on bail on conditions including that he have no contact with his victims and stay away from social media.
But Shaikh bought a new iPhone and contacted more girls.
Witness tampering
One of the charges he pleaded guilty to was luring. The victims of that offence are seven named complainants and eight unnamed, underage girls who police found evidence of on Shaikh’s new cellphone.
He also pleaded guilty to witness tampering.

Three months after his arrest, Shaikh contacted one of his victims and attempted to convince her to go to police and recant her complaint against him. He also tried to convince her that what happened between them was legal.
When given the chance to address the court, Shaikh stood up in the prisoner's box and apologized to his victims and his family.
"At the time, I failed to recognize the harm I caused to my victims," he said. "I will never truly know the extent of your pain ... I am terribly sorry to each and every one of you."
In her final words, Funk wished Shaikh luck in turning his life around after his prison term.
"What you do in that next chapter of your life will in part be up to you," said the judge.
"Through your own words, I am confident you are starting to realize the scope of damage."
